chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about hunting fish, and if one does not recite the Name of Allah over it, so he said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it necessary to say Bismillah when catching fish in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the omission of reciting *Bismillah* does not invalidate the permissibility of fish, distinguishing their status from land animals which typically require the name of Allah to be mentioned at slaughter. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic view that fish are considered 'dead' upon being caught from water, thereby simplifying the conditions for their consumption. The hadith underscores the ease (*yusr*) in dietary laws regarding aquatic life, a point of consensus among many Shia scholars.
